blocks.text: Setting up your SEO workspace on Mac

Start by creating a master database for your clients. Use the `/database` command to add a table. Add properties for Status, Deadline, and Client Name. This keeps your technical audits and content plans in one view. You can filter these views by client to avoid cluttering your dashboard.

Standardize your deliverables to save time. Create a page template for technical audits. Include sections for site speed, broken links, and metadata issues. When you start a new audit, click the arrow next to the blue New button in your database. Select your template to populate the page structure instantly.
Managing technical SEO audits in Notion

items: Create a database for crawl errors using Screaming Frog exports.
Use a select property to categorize errors by priority such as Critical, Warning, or Info.
Add a person property to assign specific fixes to your developer team.
Use a checkbox property to mark items as resolved after verification.

blocks.text: You spend a lot of time explaining technical SEO to non-technical stakeholders. Use Notion callouts to highlight key action items at the top of your reports. This ensures the most important findings are not buried in long documents. Keep your language simple and focus on business impact.

faq.question: Can I use Notion for technical SEO audits?
faq.answer: Yes. You can import CSV files from tools like Screaming Frog into Notion databases to track and prioritize technical fixes.

faq.question: Is the Notion desktop app better than the browser version?
faq.answer: The desktop app on Mac allows for better window management and keyboard shortcut consistency. It requires macOS 13 or later.
